summary: Describes how an IPv4 mobile device keeps one home address while moving between networks, using a care-of address for its current location so datagrams still reach it. It was replaced by RFC 3344.

eli5.summary: Your mail follows you if you tell the post office your temporary address while keeping your old one. This does that for a moving computer. It has been replaced by RFC 3344.

subtitle: Letting a moving computer keep its IP address by tunneling traffic to its current location.

tldr.problem: IPv4 nodes cannot change networks while keeping their IP address, forcing either renumbering (breaking connections) or routing overhead (advertising host-specific routes everywhere).
tldr.mechanism: Mobile IP lets a node keep its home address and register a care-of address at its current location. The home network intercepts datagrams destined for the mobile node and tunnels them to its current address.
tldr.outcome: Devices can move between networks without disrupting established connections. Replaced by RFC 3344 with improvements.

facts.label: Recommended movement rate
facts.value: No more than once per second

today: RFC 3220 defines Mobile IPv4 as a Proposed Standard, but was superseded by RFC 3344, which refined the protocol with numerous improvements and became the preferred specification. IPv6 has its own mobility protocol specified separately.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Internet Protocol version 4 assumes that a node's address identifies its location on the network. When a computer moves to a different network, it must change its IP address or else datagrams destined for it cannot be delivered. This breaks established connections and is unworkable for mobile devices.

Mobile IP solves this by letting a node maintain a permanent home address while abroad. When away from home, the node obtains a temporary care-of address that reflects its current location. A special router at home intercepts traffic destined for the mobile node's home address and tunnels it to the care-of address, where the mobile node receives it.
sections.eli5: You keep your home address always. When you travel, you get a temporary address for where you are. Your home router knows to forward your mail there.

sections.title: Architecture and Key Roles
sections.content:
Mobile IP introduces three new functional entities. A mobile node is a host or router that changes its point of attachment to the Internet while maintaining its home address. It may be a laptop, smartphone, or any device that travels between networks.

A home agent is a router on the mobile node's home network that intercepts datagrams destined for the mobile node and tunnels them to its current location. It maintains a list of where each of its registered mobile nodes currently is.

A foreign agent is a router on a visited network that helps mobile nodes register with their home agent and optionally serves as the endpoint of the tunnel, receiving tunneled datagrams and delivering them to the mobile node. Foreign agents also help establish connectivity between mobile nodes and other hosts on the visited network.

A mobile node acquires a care-of address in two ways: either as the address of a foreign agent (which allows multiple mobile nodes to share the same address), or as a local address obtained by the mobile node itself, such as through DHCP.
sections.eli5: Three kinds of routers work together. Your home router knows to intercept your mail. A router at your current location helps you register and receive your mail. You are the mobile computer, and you tell your home router where to send things.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
Mobile IP operates in several steps. First, agent discovery allows mobility agents to advertise their services on each link using extended ICMP Router Advertisement messages. A newly arrived mobile node can listen for these advertisements or send a solicitation to discover whether any agents are present.

When a mobile node detects that it is on its home network, it operates normally without any mobility services. When it detects movement to a foreign network, it obtains a care-of address and proceeds to register that address with its home agent.

The registration process involves a three-way exchange. The mobile node sends a Registration Request to its home agent, either directly or through a foreign agent. The Registration Request includes the care-of address and may include authentication information. The home agent sends a Registration Reply confirming or rejecting the registration.

Once registered, datagrams sent to the mobile node's home address are intercepted by the home agent, encapsulated in an IP tunnel, and forwarded to the care-of address. At the tunnel endpoint, the original datagram is extracted and delivered to the mobile node. In the reverse direction, the mobile node sends datagrams using its home address as the source, and standard IP routing delivers them to their destination.
sections.eli5: When you arrive at a new network, you tell your home router where you are. Your home router then wraps up any messages intended for you and sends them to your new location. You send your own messages out normally.

sections.title: Messages and Extensions
sections.content:
Mobile IP defines a small set of messages sent using UDP port 434. The primary messages are Registration Request and Registration Reply, which exchange registration information between mobile nodes and home agents.

The protocol uses an extensible message format that allows optional information to be carried by appending extensions. Three types of extensions are defined: a simple Type-Length-Value format for basic extensions, a long format for extensions larger than 256 bytes, and a short format that allows extension subtypes to conserve the numbering space.

Agent Advertisement and Agent Solicitation messages extend ICMP Router Discovery messages to advertise mobility agent services. Extensions in Agent Advertisements indicate which functions an agent provides (home agent, foreign agent, or both) and any care-of addresses offered, along with support for encapsulation methods and reverse tunneling.
sections.eli5: Computers send little messages in a standard format with optional add-ons. The messages tell each other where they are and confirm that messages have been registered.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
All Mobile IP control messages are authenticated using cryptographic techniques to protect against attacks. The protocol defines authentication extensions that can be attached to Registration Requests and Replies to prove that the sender is who it claims to be.

Mobile IP requires protection against replay attacks (an attacker resending old registration messages to cause misrouting). The protocol offers two mechanisms: timestamp-based replay protection, which requires synchronized clocks, and nonce-based protection, which uses a random challenge from the home agent.

The protocol also addresses privacy concerns and requires proper ingress filtering at the boundaries between networks to prevent packets with forged source addresses from entering the Internet. Key management for the authentication keys is outside the scope of the specification.
sections.eli5: Messages are signed so nobody can pretend to be you or fool your home router. The system protects against old messages being replayed to cause problems.
